query: For the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain why their mechanical properties differ during deformation and failure when constituent count alone is inadequate? Specify a controlled comparison, predictions relative to the quinary baseline, the applicable boundary conditions, supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Differences in mechanical behavior among the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary derivatives arise from composition-dependent variations in local lattice distortion (quantified by DFT-calculated MSAD) that alter dislocation glide resistance. In particular, the alloys containing Cr display larger MSAD and higher intrinsic strength (extrapolated 0 K CRSS), while those with higher proportions of Mn and Fe exhibit more pronounced dynamic solute pinning (Portevin–Le Chatelier effect) at elevated temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogenized, water-quenched, equiatomic FCC single crystals (of quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, as well as Cr-Mn-Co-Ni, Cr-Fe-Ni, Mn-Fe-Ni, Mn-Co-Ni, and Fe-Co-Ni variants) produced by Bridgman or optical floating-zone methods and annealed for 168 h at 1273 or 1473 K, machined into [1̄23]-oriented 2 × 2 × 5 mm³ compression specimens.
generation.intervention: Compression testing along [1̄23] to determine the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) for (111)[1̄01] slip at controlled temperatures (9–1373 K), strain-rate jumps over 1 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-2 s^-1 in the low-strain regime, complemented by TEM imaging of dislocations and DFT calculations of mean-square atomic displacement (MSAD).
generation.conditions: Compression tests conducted from cryogenic (below room temperature) up to 1373 K, with measurements taken outside the temperature intervals dominated by dislocation inertia (<60–77 K) and above 873 K where PL effects begin. Strain levels of ~10% plastic strain (Stage I deformation) serve as the baseline for CRSS determination.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions quantified by MSAD, which vary with alloying element content. Alloys containing Cr have larger MSAD and thus a higher resistance to dislocation glide, whereas Mn and Fe, through diffusible solute effects, promote dynamic solute pinning at high temperatures.
generation.mechanism: At temperatures below room temperature, dislocation glide is primarily governed by thermally activated overcoming of solid-solution obstacles—the local lattice distortion provides the energy landscape that impedes glide. At elevated temperatures (673–873 K and above), diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres elastically interact with moving dislocations, causing a Portevin–Le Chatelier-type serrated flow. Cr-induced lattice distortion raises the 0 K extrapolated CRSS, and the extent of PL strengthening scales with the Mn plus Fe content.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the quinary baseline, alloys with higher Cr content (hence larger MSAD) should demonstrate increased extrapolated 0 K CRSS, while those enriched in Mn and Fe should show a more pronounced PL effect with a modest CRSS increase and serrated flow at high temperatures. Additionally, as temperature decreases below room temperature, CRSS should substantially increase (due to reduced thermal activation), but the rate of increase will diminish below about 77 K due to inertial effects.
generation.baseline: The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloy, with its room-temperature CRSS and intermediate high-temperature (673–873 K) behavior before pronounced PL effects appear, serves as the reference composition and temperature regime.
generation.boundary: This mechanistic hypothesis applies to equiatomic FCC single crystals of Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni systems produced by Bridgman or optical floating-zone methods, tested in compression along [1̄23] under the specified thermal and strain-rate conditions. It is valid in the temperature regimes below the inertial-dominated region (<60–77 K) and below the full PL-dominated regime (above ~873 K), where conventional thermal-activation models are applicable.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative scaling of MSAD with CRSS and the exact contribution of the PL effect might vary with unaccounted factors such as potential magnetic transitions or other subtle microstructural effects; therefore, while the direction of change is supported, the magnitude of these effects remains uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform temperature-dependent compression tests on the series of equiatomic alloys while systematically varying composition to isolate the effects of Cr versus Mn/Fe content. Measure CRSS from the 0.2% offset yield stress across the range from cryogenic to high temperatures, complemented by strain-rate jump tests to capture inertial and PL regimes. Utilize TEM to examine dislocation configurations (e.g., partial dislocation dissociation) at room and high temperatures, and correlate DFT-computed MSAD with the extrapolated 0 K CRSS values.
measurements: Temperature-dependent CRSS (0.2% offset yield stress) under compression along [1̄23]
Strain-rate sensitivity and activation volume from strain-rate jumps
Observation of stress–strain serrations (PL behavior) at elevated temperatures
TEM analysis of dislocation structures and partial dislocation dissociation widths
DFT calculations of MSAD for each alloy composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured extrapolated 0 K CRSS does not correlate with the computed MSAD (i.e., alloys with higher MSAD do not consistently exhibit higher CRSS) or if the predicted differences in PL behavior (serrated flow and CRSS increment for Mn/Fe-rich alloys) relative to the quinary baseline are not observed, then the hypothesis is rejected.
